MAIN PROTEIN, and the batch's loudest line - read the cross-check. Source prints BOTH a count (5 links) and a weight range ('about 1.5-2 pounds' = 136-181 g/link). Booked at the LOW END of the printed range: 1.5 lb x 2.8 = 4.2 lb = 1905 g (14 links at 136 g), because (a) an explicit printed weight outranks every other basis (fricassee/tandoori rule), and (b) the source's own published 561 cal recomputes to +0.6% on exactly this reading. CONFLICTING BASES DISCLOSED: densities each = 90 g (14 links = 1260 g -> 439 cal/serving) matches the source's published 28 g protein instead; today's board captures say retail 5-link packs are 19 oz (Walmart Marketside '5 Links, 1 lb 3 oz', Aldi 19 oz) = 108 g/link -> 1512 g -> 488 cal/serving. All three readings land in band; the printed-weight anchor is the ruling. italian-sausage commodity covers hot and mild in one price class, 6 of 7 stores, cheapest Aldi $2.4842/lb. The Hot Italian Sausage DB row's raw-vs-cooked basis ambiguity (flagged by italian-sausage-peppers-onions-skillet, unresolved) applies here too: a raw-basis correction would ADD roughly 100 cal/serving and push this recipe to ~665, just OVER the 650 ceiling - this recipe must not publish until that row's basis is pinned by the meal-macro label check the skillet batch requested.

macro_cross_check.verdict: CALLED OUT LOUDLY - the protein instrument BREAKS at +35.4%, and for once the finding is against the SOURCE, not a portion: their own printed sausage line ('5 links, about 1.5-2 pounds') makes 28 g protein/serving unreachable - 1.5 lb of Italian sausage plus a full stick and an ounce of mozzarella per serving computes 37.9 P minimum, while their 28 P back-solves to ~85-90 g links, flatly contradicting their own printed weight. Their calories agree with their printed weight (our 565.0 vs their 561, +0.7% on the 1.5 lb low end), so the incoherence lives in their protein/fat fields (fat 46 likewise fits no consistent reading). Portions here follow the printed weight; the published protein figure is recorded as unreliable. Every candidate basis (90/108/136 g links) computes in-band: 439/488/565.
macro_cross_check.band_check: computed 565.0 cal in [400, 650] PASS (85 of ceiling headroom) - BUT CONDITIONAL: the Hot Italian Sausage DB row's unresolved raw-vs-cooked basis (see sausage line note) would add ~100 cal/serving on the raw-basis reading and breach the ceiling at ~665. Do not publish until the sausage row's basis is pinned; carbs 14.7 g <= 35 PASS either way.
